entries.reason: TargetingResolver consumes ISensingCandidateProvider through cap::query and the new script seam answers it through cap::provide, so the same capability appears on both faces; recording them makes the next provider declare itself instead of silently displacing the single-provider slot. The scope is this one file, not src/modules/sensing/**: the fact mirror, the ranking pipeline and the script world bindings expose different faces.
binds: eve.provider.publishFor('eve.sensing.ISensingCandidateProvider', name, instance) -> queryCandidates({ origin, space, originLocation, domain, minRange, maxRange, requiredTags, excludedTags, zone, area }) returning an array of { subject, location = { space, x, y, z }, domain, tags, zones }
entries.thread_affinity: Sensing owner thread; queryCandidates answers one synchronous script call and returns an owning array, retaining no VM value

trim.absent_profile: Profiles without sensing leave ISensingCandidateProvider unbound; targeting falls back to the in-tree provider set and the script seam simply is not registered

cost_notes: queryCandidates marshals one candidate array per query and the ranking pipeline calls it once per resolver pass, so the cost is proportional to the returned candidate count.

entries.reason: The sensing module instance publishes ISensingQuery for its fact mirror, the same capability the targeting resolver consumes, so a second provider or consumer must declare itself instead of silently displacing the single-provider slot.
entries.thread_affinity: Sensing owner thread; queries read the fact mirror synchronously and retain no callback or script value.

trim.absent_profile: Profiles without sensing leave ISensingQuery unbound; consumers that queried it fall back to their documented absent behavior.
